text:
Anya: Seeing a cluster-wide issue: a handful of GPU nodes in the dedicated fleet can't pull images — kubelet keeps erroring with ErrImagePull and pods stay in ImagePullBackOff. Noticed it right after a scale-up.

Anya: manual pull on the node times out:
```
# docker pull registry.internal.redwood.com/runtime/gpu:2026-03
Trying to pull ...
ERROR: Get "https://registry.internal.redwood.com/v2/": net/http: TLS handshake timeout
```

Kevin: Which subnet are those nodes in? any difference in NACLs or route tables vs the other pools?

Anya: They're in subnet prod-gpu-3 (AZ b). Other nodepools (cpu and staging gpu) fine. SG egress is wide open to 0.0.0.0/0:443, but I can't reach the registry from the node.

Samir: Can you run a tcpdump while reproducing? I want to see whether SYNs leave and whether we get replies.

Anya: Pasted tcpdump snippet:
```
22:41:02.123456 IP 10.50.7.12.49155 > 35.156.12.9.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460,sackOK,TS val 123456 ecr 0], length 0
22:41:02.123789 IP 10.50.7.12.49155 > 35.156.12.9.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [...], length 0
# no SYN-ACK seen, after retries we just get nothing
```

Samir: Huh — SYNs leaving from high source ports (49k). That smells like a NACL / stateless firewall drop on the return path. Security groups are stateful so SGs would have allowed replies, but NACLs are stateless and you need explicit inbound/outbound rules that match the ephemeral port ranges.

Maya: Only the prod-gpu-3 subnet uses the hardened NACL that we rolled out last week (tight inbound/outbound to reduce blast radius). Did that NACL change include a restricted high-port range?

Samir: Looking through the NACL rules for prod-gpu-3:
```
Rule 100: ALLOW TCP 443 0.0.0.0/0 (outbound)
Rule 110: DENY TCP 1024-65535 0.0.0.0/0 (inbound)  <-- this will block return traffic to dynamic source ports
```
Note: NACLs are evaluated by number and are stateless — replies to ephemeral client ports must be allowed in the inbound direction too.

Kevin: That explains why only these nodes (in that subnet) are affected. Image pulls originate from ephemeral/high source ports and the registry replies target those source ports. If inbound NACL denies that range, SYN-ACK gets dropped.

Anya: Confirmed via cloud NACL flow logs: a bunch of DENY entries for bytes destined to 10.50.7.12:49155 coming from 35.156.12.9:443 with rule 110.

Samir: Quick mitigation: add an explicit inbound ALLOW for TCP 1024-65535 from 0.0.0.0/0 (or restrict to registry IPs/CIDR if we want tighter scoping). Also consider limiting outbound in the NACL if required, but make sure replies are permitted.

infra-bot: Running change: aws ec2 replace-network-acl-entry --network-acl-id nacl-0a1b2c3d --rule-number 111 --protocol tcp --port-range From=1024,To=65535 --egress false --rule-action allow --cidr 0.0.0.0/0

Maya: applied the rule, propagating now.

Anya: Re-testing image pull after the change:
```
# docker pull registry.internal.redwood.com/runtime/gpu:2026-03
2026-03: Pulling from runtime/gpu
Digest: sha256:...
Status: Downloaded newer image for registry.internal:443/runtime/gpu:2026-03
```

Anya: Pods are now scheduling and kubelet pulled images fine. 

Kevin: Nice. Root cause: overly strict inbound NACL on the dedicated prod GPU subnet that blocked replies to dynamic client ports.

Samir: Postmortem / action items: 
- Update the NACL rollout checklist to include ephemeral/dynamic port ranges (1024-65535) for inbound when outbound 443/80 is allowed.
- Add an automated test in infra CI that deploys a short-lived VM in any subnet with new NACLs and verifies registry/tcp connectivity in both directions.
- Add a CloudWatch/Datadog alert for repeated ImagePullBackOff or registry TLS timeouts aggregated per subnet for 5m.
- Review whether we can scope inbound allow to known registry CIDRs instead of 0.0.0.0/0 to reduce blast radius.

Maya: I'll file the runbook PR and the test ticket.

Anya: Thanks everyone — retrospective note: this is why we need integration tests for NACL changes. :thumbsup:
